- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3+ points in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-7 days; apply downward correction of 1-2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7-10 day window and adjust forecast downward if sentiment turns negative.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; for 30-day forecasts, smooth out abrupt sentiment-driven deviations using 5-day moving average of sentiment-weighted price.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below 70), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 0.5-1.5 points per day of deviation.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance slightly (±0.5–1.0) to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
